checks: The selected circuits come from the actual restricted maxima, each through the interior of its anchor fiber. At that mark continuous balance implies h_i=A_i·z_i. The weighted sum of margins is constant on a base plane and gives whole-plane cover whenever nonnegative. The finite lattice-complete base permits Doignon compression: add conv(P) to the closed replacements of the strict complements on P and select at most 2^n convex sets whose intersection avoids the lattice. Only deepest-origin groups can cover a deepest mark. Local circuits added at nondeep sites are strictly slack.

The assigned coverage rows keep the entire corresponding plane covered after changes of v and b, because u and ρ remain fixed. Under the old budgets, any larger admissible mixed volume M' would give normalized depth at most βM/M'<β. Common continuous dilation restoring the central volume preserves normalized depth and facet counts, so the comparison is valid on the chart with variable central volume.

The normal fan of the old body is refined by its stable small-erosion fan, whose rays are the original facet normals. The linear restriction to each fiber's own fan preserves the original facet bound and leaves the old support in the chart. The accepted finite rows give exactly A₀ ḣ≥0 for forward affine paths. Adding the active linear DC_ip rows gives the joint radial cone. The common erosion lies in it: inner parallel bodies preserve anchored Minkowski inclusions, their support coordinates vary affinely for small positive time, and holding the cap coefficients fixed leaves every coverage row unchanged.

The joint strip formula can be used on a single fiber with one owner per facet. With outward speed a and cap margin speed k after division by the continuous normal norm, the inner coincidence contributes min(a,k), and the outer coincidence contributes max(a+k,0). This yields the same allocation in each cap's body and parameter terms. Proper sections have full coarea, while strict full, strict empty and lower-dimensional supporting cases have zero coarea. In dimension one the facet and section calculations count points.

A positive-volume active cap has a vertex of some fiber with strictly positive margin, so an incident facet contributes a relatively open positive-area patch strictly inside the cap. Its erosion derivative is negative in every branch. Other contributions are nonpositive since a=-1 and k=0. Adding a small positive multiple of erosion to an improving radial direction with all branches nonpositive preserves improvement and makes every active cap derivative strictly negative. The finite cone polar therefore has generators given by the cap branches and the negatives of the radial rows. Grouping coefficients gives one consistent convexified covector per cap and objective coefficient one.

The free b_ij component of the stress is 0=-λ_ij S_ij+ρ_ij t_i and the free v_ij component is 0=λ_ij Σ_z s_ijz z−ρ_ij Σ_p η_ip p. In a deepest-origin group the proper anchor section ensures S_ij>0 regardless of supporting allocations elsewhere. The slack group has all cap multipliers zero and then t_i=0 by the offset equation. For t_i>0 the two equations give the common section-base mean, and active coverage gives A_i·z̄_i=h_i. Substitution produces t_i(h_i−A_i·z̄_i)=0 in the signed offset sum.

Under joint dilation, let the coincidence satisfy u·x=b−v·z. The cap speed is k=(v·z−b)/||u||. In the inside case n_F=−u/||u|| gives a=k, and in the outside case n_F=u/||u|| gives a=−k. Thus every branch evaluates to the actual dilation derivative. Both the active A₀ rows and the active coverage rows evaluate to zero by homogeneity. Since each stressed cap has mass βM, evaluating gives dM=dβM Σλ and the claimed reciprocal identity.

The frozen claim matches source 5e600a897e2488c6:03 §§2–3 and §5. It keeps the individual bounded-facet chart and uses the active equality A_i·z̄_i=h_i, which also covers the degenerate case A_i=h_i=0.

dependencies.hypotheses: A finite collection of convex sets has intersection missing Z^n after adding conv(P) to the closed halfspaces realizing the complementary traces on finite P. The selected lattice-infeasible subfamily has at most 2^n members. The bound is also explicitly stated in Aliev, Bassett, De Loera and Louveaux, A Quantitative Doignon–Bell–Scarf Theorem, https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2480.
dependencies.reference: Jean-Paul Doignon, Convexity in cristallographical lattices (1973), lattice Helly theorem

overlap.comparison: Provides the same bounded-facet minimizer, individual-fan chart and common erosion. Its caps are held fixed, so it supplies neither the free offset and tilt equations nor groupwise cancellation of its signed Euler term.

The accepted shared-plane rotating-cap theorem proves the same scalar normalization and base-moment equations and adds a continuous-moment equation in that class. Its free common body-plane coefficients and shared list bound do not establish an identity on the individual-fan radial cone for a general per-fiber bounded-facet minimizer. The frozen proof supplies that case with fixed continuous cap normals.
Gives the initial projected whole-plane group selection and a separate fixed-normal quantile continuation. It does not supply joint radial stationarity in free base tilts and offsets.

readability: On the dilation direction the phrase about active homogeneous rows includes the convex-support rows of A₀ as well as the compatibility and coverage rows. The proof already establishes homogeneity for each.
review_method: Independent cold reading of the frozen statement and proof followed by direct source, predecessor, and exact sign checks.
summary: The bounded-facet chart permits the joint volume comparison and finite polar argument. The resulting objective-one stress gives the two section-base moments, the groupwise offset cancellation, and the exact normalization.
